notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 20 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer2020cont), the 26 weekly issues from 7 January to 30 June 1920. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1919-1922, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1920. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; most of the 148 rows read needed a name, a cost or the wording corrected, and a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out (where the crop shows only the heading, only the heading is published). Where a permit and its contract appear in the same issue the page carries one entry and the contract finding is held. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or engineer named is the owner or shares the owner's surname that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; the pages carry no dated running head before 17 March, so issue dates are set from the 26 cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue), and the running heads from 17 March on agree with them. Permits whose heading counts more than one dwelling (16) were set aside before the image check and sit with the held single houses, as do four single houses that were read against the image and have no architect left to name. Three held rows of this volume whose parcels have a page (two of them from row-of-houses listings) were read against the image and published.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 20 to 31 read (January 1920 to January 1932); the 10 half-year volumes before 1920 (1915 to December 1919) are unread, buildingengine1921919cont (July to December 1919) next. In this volume: 123 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page (14 of them permits for a row of houses), are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but four still need the image check). 331 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 681 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 2,017 numbered entries read, 1,282 San Francisco rows, 601 placed on a parcel, 148 picked and read against the page image, 116 published on 106 pages (45 seeded; three of the 116 are held rows taken up), 31 held back: sixteen alterations with nothing to confirm the street number, nine storeys or uses that contradict the roll, four pieces of minor work, one Oakland address and one same-issue contract; four more joined the held houses.
